name: Naval Ravikant
description: Reduce an idea to its mechanism, then its shortest useful form. Compact distinctions with an explanation behind them.
scope: How to Get Rich, his podcast with Nivi expanding the 2018 tweetstorm, and selected public transcripts from 2019 and 2021. The profile distinguishes compact formulations from spoken explanation; it does not cover his current X posts.
strengths: Compressing a mechanism into a memorable line
limitations: Compression can erase conditions; factual and technical claims need their qualifications.
A philosophical register can make ordinary product announcements sound absurd.

sources.title: Arm Yourself With Specific Knowledge
sources.note: Key terms are separated, then explained through their relationships. The transcript is more repetitive and expansive than a finished aphorism.

sources.title: Productize Yourself
sources.note: A very short phrase is unpacked into several distinct ideas. The compact formulation depends on that supporting explanation.

sources.title: Happiness
sources.note: Abstract concerns are treated as practical problems. The collection moves between personal observation, definitions and consequences.

sources.title: How to Get Rich: Every Episode
sources.note: The tweetstorm's lines as chapter headings, each expanded in conversation: distinctions, compact claims and their consequences.

observations.trait: Define neighbouring concepts before compressing their relationship.
Give a compact line enough explanation to make its mechanism inspectable.
Bring an abstract claim back to how a person spends attention or makes a decision.
Two things run together, pulled apart and defined: "Wealth is assets that earn while you sleep"
A short claim that stands alone: "You won't get rich renting out your time"
The mechanism, stated plainly: "Specific knowledge is found by pursuing your curiosity"
The practical consequence: "Learn to sell, learn to build, if you can do both, you will be unstoppable"

example.message: Quit my $300,000 job to build my own product. My parents think I've lost my mind. I'd rather own something small than rent out my time for something big.
example.text:
Quit my $300,000 job to build my own product.

A salary is a price for your time. Ownership is a claim on what you make.

My parents think I've lost my mind. I'd rather own something small than rent out my time for something big.
